scope: Static peer review of completed native player-prefix writer and immutable reopened observations
confirmed_design: Reopen binds the database and four audit hashes, exact audit frame counts and sequential frame indices before accepting the prefix.
Typed selected boxes, source proposal indices, registration matrices and candidate records are reconstructed as detached snapshots; header/crop/initial observations also return detached data.
Reopened SQLite is read-only, query-only and immutable; per-row digest and producer shape/type checks run on requested frames.
Header, initial and frame component lengths are checked in SQL before the corresponding payload fetch; SQLite also limits record length.
Previously reported cursor masking is fixed with primary-error-preserving close; schema retrieval now counts and bounds objects and columns.

findings.trigger: On the non-Windows directory-sync branch, fsync raises a BaseException and os.close also raises.
findings.observed_behavior: The finally-close replaces the original fsync exception.
findings.impact: Primary failure identity is lost during prefix seal publication cleanup. Current Windows execution does not enter this branch.
findings.minimal_fix: Use except/else descriptor cleanup, attach close failure as a note to the original fsync error, and re-raise the original.
findings.suggested_regression: Inject fsync KeyboardInterrupt plus descriptor-close failure in a controlled POSIX-branch unit fixture; verify original identity and attached cleanup note.
